questions.correct: Showing what your code is doing on the Driver Hub
wrong: Reversing a motor that spins the wrong way
Charging the robot's battery between two matches
Storing your code package as a zip file
questions.explain: telemetry prints labels and values to the Driver Hub screen. It's the most useful tool for seeing what your code is really doing while it runs.

questions.correct: Queues one line with a label and a value
wrong: Immediately shows the line on the screen
Deletes the last line that was printed
Reverses the spin direction of a motor
questions.explain: addData queues one line (label on the left, value on the right). It doesn't actually appear until telemetry.update() is called.

questions.correct: Actually shows the queued lines on the screen
wrong: Adds one more blank line to the telemetry
Clears all of the code out of the editor
Restarts the robot's main run loop
questions.explain: addData writes lines to a notepad; update() holds the notepad up to the driver. Without update(), the queued lines never appear.

questions.correct: A labeled box that holds one value
wrong: A recipe of steps you run by name
A wire from the hub to a motor
A button press from the controller
questions.explain: A variable is a labeled box holding a value. The name stays the same while the contents can change — like loops holding a count that climbs.

questions.q: What kind of number does an int hold?
questions.correct: Whole numbers only, with no decimal point
wrong: Numbers with a decimal point, like 1.5
Only the two values true and false
Text, such as words and letters
questions.explain: An int holds whole numbers (integers) only — no decimals. For values like 1.5 you'd use a double instead.

questions.correct: Add one to the loops variable
wrong: Reset the loops variable to one
Print the loops value to the screen
Delete the loops variable entirely
questions.explain: loops += 1; is shorthand for "add one to loops." Put it in the loop and the counter climbs by one every pass.

questions.q: In telemetry.addData, what does the dot mean?
questions.correct: Ask this thing to do that action
wrong: Multiply the two sides together
End the current line of code
Start a brand-new code package
questions.explain: The dot means "ask this thing to do that." telemetry.addData reads as "telemetry, add this data." It's how you call a method on something.

questions.q: Where must a counting variable be declared to keep its value?
questions.correct: Outside the loop, so it isn't reset each pass
wrong: Inside the loop, so it starts fresh each pass
After the class's final closing brace
Inside the import lines at the very top
questions.explain: A variable declared inside the loop is wiped and reset every pass. Declare it outside (above) the loop so its value survives between loops and can climb.

questions.q: How often does loop code run?
wrong: About once every 50 seconds
Exactly one time per whole match
Only when a button is pressed
questions.explain: The run loop repeats roughly 50 times a second. A counter incremented in the loop climbs fast — proof your code is really running.

questions.correct: Once, right when the program starts
wrong: About 50 times every single second
Only when the battery is fully charged
Backward, after the loop has finished
questions.explain: Init code runs once at the start. Loop code, inside the while braces, repeats ~50 times a second. Knowing which is which is key.

questions.q: Why watch a loop counter climb on telemetry?
questions.correct: It proves the loop is running, like a heartbeat
wrong: It makes the drive motors spin much faster
It charges the battery a little each loop
It permanently saves the code to a disk
questions.explain: A counter that climbs every loop is the loop's heartbeat — it visually proves your code is alive and looping, which is great for debugging.

questions.q: What appears on the left of a telemetry line?
questions.correct: The label you gave to addData
wrong: The number of loops so far
The robot's battery percentage
The name of your code package
questions.explain: addData("label", value) shows the label on the left and the value on the right — for example "Loops" on the left and the count on the right.

questions.q: What happens if you forget telemetry.update()?
questions.correct: Your queued lines never show on the screen
wrong: The robot immediately stops all its motors
The code fails to build at all
The counter resets itself back to zero
questions.explain: Without update(), the lines you added stay on the notepad and are never shown. update() is what pushes them to the Driver Hub.

questions.q: What ends most lines of Java code?
wrong: A period
A comma
A colon
questions.explain: Most Java statements end with a semicolon (;). A missing one is a common reason a build fails.

questions.q: A value that must survive between loops should be...
wrong: Declared new inside the loop
Printed and then thrown away
Stored in a separate zip file
questions.explain: Declare it above the loop so it's created once and keeps its value each pass. Declaring it inside the loop resets it every single time.
